data.title: Dream-Up
data.content: Image generator from DeviantArt based on the Stable Diffusion model. Includes opt-out options for creators who are native to DeviantArt, and credit lines when their style is used, though the credibility of this mechanism has been contested given the integral training of the SD model. DeviantArt offer little insight into the design of their full stack and have produced considerable controversy within their own long-established community.

data.title: Have I been Trained API
data.content: API developed by Spawning for developers to audit opt-outs for training (see entry for Have I been Trained?). Operates as additional layer of scrutiny.

data.title: Have I been Trained?
data.content: User-facing tool which can instantly search AI training databases using 'clip retreival' to find out if your data has been used to train ML models which use the predominant Laion-5B and Laion-400M image datasets. This is a highly interoperable tool designed to be deployed in the onward scrutiny of datasets used to train commercial models. Though the tool's own code in not open source, it acts as a plug-in to increase the transparency of other tools, making public value core to its function.

data.title: Stable Diffusion
data.content: Stable Diffusion is an open source text-to-image latent diffusion model created by the researchers and engineers from CompVis, Stability AI and LAION. It's trained on 512x512 images from a subset of the LAION-5B database. This model uses a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 text encoder to condition the model on text prompts. The model is relatively lightweight and can run on many consumer GPUs.Stability integrate an 'AI-based Safety Classifier' by default. This filters undesirable features from the output, though 'the parameters of this can be readily adjusted' and the classifier may be adapted based on community feedback. The integration of this classifier, combined with Stability's focus on technical transparency, makes SD the most scrutenisable of the highly effecatious T2I models.

data.title: Midjourney 5.2
data.content: Midjourney operates a prompt-to-image generative service, taking Discord as it's user interface. It offers little detail on the architecture or exact training protocol, though reportedly it is trained at least in part on LAION-5B. Though it produces high-fidelity images with consistently-recognisable Midjourney 'default' style, recent v5.2 includes a fine-tuning parameter to minimise this. Midjourney operate a takedown request policy, allowing creatives to request their work be removed from training sets. Paid members to Midjourney services own their generated assets. Non-paying users are granted use under a Creative Commons Noncommercial 4.0 Attribution International License. Within the parameters of this license, a user can make use of Midjourney-generated assets in onward workflows, though the tool itself is not technically interoperable, offering no official API.
